questions.q: According to Brach, where does our feeling of inadequacy come from?
a: Cultural messages teaching that we are not enough
A chemical imbalance present from birth
A lack of discipline in our daily routines
Comparisons we make only in adulthood
questions.why: Lesson 1 traces the feeling to Western culture and stories that say we must redeem ourselves.

questions.q: What happened to Mohini the tiger in the summary?
a: She paced a small area inside a much larger enclosure
She refused to leave her original cage
She escaped and returned to the wild
She grew aggressive toward her keepers
questions.why: Lesson 2 says her mind kept her in the old cage long after the zoo gave her space to roam.

questions.q: What does self-judgment do, according to the summary?
a: It covers up feelings like fear and vulnerability
It sharpens your ability to make decisions
It protects other people from your emotions
It replaces sadness with calm acceptance
questions.why: Lesson 3 describes self-blame as a defence that hides jealousy, fear and vulnerability.

questions.q: How does Brach suggest healing emotional pain?
a: By fully feeling suffering with compassion
By distracting yourself with achievements
By reasoning your way out of the feeling
By waiting for the feeling to pass
questions.why: Lesson 3 says healing begins when we experience suffering instead of judging or pushing it away.

questions.q: How does Buddhism view human nature, in contrast with Western culture?
a: People are naturally loving and wise, not flawed
People are born sinful and must earn grace
People are shaped entirely by their surroundings
People cannot change after early childhood
questions.why: Lesson 1 says Buddhism sees humans as naturally loving and wise rather than sinful.
